concept.name: Rolling standard deviation
concept.definition: The rolling standard deviation is the sample (or population) standard deviation of a series over a trailing window of fixed length that slides forward one observation at a time. Applied to returns it is the standard estimator of realized volatility and the width driver of Bollinger Bands.
concept.intuition: It measures how spread out the last N returns (or prices) were — a live gauge of how violently the market has been moving recently.
concept.mechanics: For window w, compute σ over the last w observations at each step; pandas rolling(window).std() uses the sample (unbiased, ddof=1) convention by default and labels at the window's right edge. On returns, annualization scales by √T (e.g., √252 for daily data).
concept.formula: σ_t = sqrt( (1/(w−1)) Σ_{i=0}^{w−1} (x_{t−i} − μ_t)² ), where μ_t is the rolling mean over the same window (use 1/w for the population convention).
concept.failure_modes: The estimate assumes the window's observations come from one stable regime; volatility clustering makes short windows noisy and long windows slow to react. Squaring returns gives extreme observations outsized influence, and with w−1 denominators small windows are unreliable.
concept.misconceptions: Rolling std of prices is not comparable across instruments or time as price levels drift — volatility is conventionally computed on returns, not price levels.
concept.example: The 20-day rolling std of daily log returns at 0.015 (1.5%) annualizes to roughly 0.015 × √252 ≈ 23.8%.
